title: A Group Chat for the Semester
premise: Felix Crane, seventeen and effectively the parent of his two younger siblings, has built his whole life on staying invisible — until a college application essay prompt ('What is the worst thing you've ever done?') leaks into a shared group chat and forces five classmates to answer honestly, including Felix's confession about the night he covered for someone he shouldn't have. The chat becomes a pressure cooker of secrets, bargains, and blackmail as each member realizes what the others now hold over them. To survive senior year, Felix must lead a ragtag academic decathlon team to a championship nobody cares about while protecting his family from the fallout of the truth — and in the final week, he must choose between winning the scholarship that could save them and exposing the lie that keeps the group's most powerful member safe. He tells the truth, loses the scholarship, and discovers that loyalty built on silence was never loyalty at all.
about_author: Casper Ravensworth is the pen name of a former debate coach who spent six years watching teenagers say true things they couldn't take back. They write in a converted garage in Ohio, where the group chat never stops buzzing.

chapters.title: Head Down, Grades Up
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. A day in the life: waking his siblings Dara and Milo, packing lunches, acing a chemistry quiz, and dodging every invitation to belong. Establishes the invisible architecture of his survival and the quiet pride he takes in it. Emotional beat: controlled loneliness that feels like competence.

chapters.title: The Prompt
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. In college counseling, the essay prompt 'What is the worst thing you've ever done?' lands on his desk like an accusation. His counselor insists honesty wins scholarships; Felix knows honesty costs them. That night, on a whim and half-asleep, he types one true sentence into a new group chat with four classmates assigned to peer-review essays. Beat: the first crack in the wall.

chapters.title: Five Strangers, One Thread
chapters.summary: Rotating POV. The chat members introduce themselves through what they refuse to say: Priya, the perfect daughter; Marcus, the star quarterback hiding a concussion; Wren, the artist who saw something she shouldn't have; Dev, the class clown whose jokes are armor. Each posts a sanitized essay. Felix notices everyone is lying. Beat: uneasy alliance formed.

chapters.title: What Felix Wrote
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. At 2 a.m., unable to sleep, Felix pastes the truth: the night he took the blame for a hit-and-run he didn't commit to protect someone whose name he still won't type. He deletes it in nine seconds — but screenshots exist. Beat: terror, then the strange relief of having said it once.

chapters.title: The Screenshot Economy
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya admits she kept Felix's deleted message and shows him why: her father's campaign depends on her perfection, and she needs leverage too. She proposes a pact — everyone's worst thing stays in the vault unless someone breaks the rules. Felix hates it and agrees. Beat: the price of survival becomes literal currency.

chapters.title: Locker Shut
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Mom picks up double shifts at the hospital; Milo gets sick; Felix misses the first academic decathlon practice and is voluntold into joining because the team needs one more body to qualify. The coach is desperate; the team is a joke. Beat: resentment curdling into reluctant responsibility.

chapters.title: Marcus Breaks
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Playing through a second concussion, Marcus fumbles the championship qualifier and his father's rage goes public in the parking lot. He confesses in the chat that the hit-and-run Felix covered for was Marcus's — and that Marcus's dad paid to bury it. Beat: the vault cracks open from inside.

chapters.title: The One Who Knew
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren reveals she witnessed the accident and stayed silent because Marcus's family funded her art scholarship. Her guilt has been eating her for a year. Felix realizes three people in the chat are chained to the same night. Beat: pity and fury tangled together.

chapters.title: Dev's Bargain
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Dev, it turns out, runs the school's rumor economy and offers to scrub the story — for a price: Felix's spot as team captain, which comes with a scholarship nomination. Dev isn't cruel, just transactional; his own secret (forged transcripts) gives him skin in the game. Beat: power changes hands without a fight.

chapters.title: Dinner With Strangers
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Mom finally gets a night off and asks one real question about Felix's life; he can't answer honestly without unraveling everything. Dara catches him crying over the essay draft and, twelve years old, says the truest line in the book: 'You're allowed to be a kid too.' Beat: devastating tenderness.

chapters.title: Practice Makes Liars
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Decathlon practice is chaos — Marcus can't study with headaches, Wren won't speak, Dev sabotages drills. Felix, against his nature, starts leading: assigning topics, calling out excuses, making the misfits a unit. Beat: the slow discovery that he's good at being seen.

chapters.title: Priya's Perfect Crime
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya's father finds her draft essay — about the pact, anonymized — and recognizes the shape of scandal. He orders her to hand over the screenshots to 'manage' the situation. She copies them but hesitates to send. Beat: the corrupting offer, delivered with love.

chapters.title: The Leak
chapters.summary: Rotating POV. Fragments of the chat surface anonymously — not the hit-and-run yet, but enough: Marcus's medical file, Dev's transcripts, Wren's scholarship terms. The school launches an investigation. Everyone suspects everyone. Beat: paranoia as weather; trust dissolves.

chapters.title: Interrogation Light
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The vice principal interviews Felix, dangling the scholarship nomination as reward for naming names. Felix says nothing, protecting people who may have betrayed him. Walking out, he realizes silence — his oldest skill — is now serving the wrong side. Beat: loyalty vs. truth begins its real argument.

chapters.title: Regionals
chapters.summary: Felix and Marcus POV alternating. Against all odds, the team qualifies for regionals; Marcus plays his first clean match sober from football, and the group feels briefly like a family. Then Priya's father's lawyer contacts Felix directly: sign a statement implicating Marcus, and the Crane kids' futures are 'taken care of.' Beat: temptation wearing a helpful face.

chapters.title: The Vault Opens
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren, unable to carry it, tells the truth to the police about the hit-and-run — not to hurt Marcus, but because she can't be bought twice. Marcus turns himself in with his parents furious and broken. The pact is dead; the chat goes silent. Beat: grief for a friendship that honesty killed and saved simultaneously.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Actually Is
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix visits Marcus before his hearing. No speeches — just two kids admitting they were both protecting the wrong things. Marcus asks Felix to tell the whole story at the hearing, including Felix's false confession. Beat: forgiveness without absolution; the theme stated in action, not words.

chapters.title: The Championship That Doesn't Matter
chapters.summary: Full team POV rotation. State decathlon finals: the misfit team nobody scouted competes with nothing left to hide, and it makes them fearless. They win by two points on Felix's final essay read aloud — the honest one. Beat: triumph that feels like exhaling after drowning.

chapters.title: The Last Game of the Season
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The championship that does matter: Marcus's disciplinary hearing, where Felix testifies to everything — his false confession, the cover-up, the money. The room shifts; consequences land where they should, including on Felix for lying to police. Beat: the climax — truth chosen at maximum cost.

chapters.title: Sentences
chapters.summary: Rotating POV. Fallout: Marcus gets diversion and community service; Felix accepts a suspended record and loses the nomination; Dev, quietly, uses his rumor network one last time to get Felix's story to a journalist — and a local scholarship fund for 'students raising siblings' appears. Priya burns her father's leverage publicly. Beat: justice imperfect but real.

chapters.title: The Essay, Final Draft
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix rewrites his college essay with no secrets left to spend, answering the prompt plainly: the worst thing he ever did was disappear to survive, and the best was learning to be seen. Dara reads it over his shoulder and approves. Beat: quiet catharsis; identity rebuilt around truth instead of silence.

chapters.title: A Group Chat for the Summer
chapters.summary: Felix's POV, epilogue. The chat renames itself; the five meet at the diner where Wren's scholarship dinner once excluded them all. Mom works days now. Nothing is fixed — money is tight, records are stained — but Felix walks into school with his locker open. Beat: earned hope; the price was paid, and it was worth it.
